runbook_template.name: Pressurized Main Tie-In — Generic Shutdown Runbook
runbook_template.notes: Generic sequence for a cut-in tie-in to an existing pressurized water main during a negotiated shutdown window. T+0 = start of shutdown window (window_start). Durations are placeholders — the whole point of the planning view is that the team edits these against the negotiated window and the district reviews the total. Assumes district operations personnel operate district-owned valves; confirm and adjust responsible_party per district. For sewer force main or gravity tie-ins, swap disinfection steps for bypass/plugging steps.

pre_window_steps.description: Shutdown request submitted to district with plan, sequence, and materials list; window negotiated
Pothole/expose existing main; verify OD, material, and condition against fittings on hand
All fittings, couplings, restraint hardware, and spare parts on site and verified against potholed dimensions
District confirms isolation valves have been exercised and hold (or provides plan for valves that don't)
Customer/public notifications issued per district requirements
Pre-shutdown meeting: sequence walked step-by-step with district ops, inspector, crew; contingency triggers and abort criteria agreed
Disinfection materials ready (hypochlorite solution for swabbing/spraying per C651 tie-in method); dechlorination and dewatering BMPs staged
Excavation dewatered, shored, competent-person inspection logged; work area lit (night work) and access clear

window_steps.description: Window opens — all parties on site confirmed (district operator, inspector, crew, standby). Go/no-go decision.
District operates isolation valves per agreed sequence (record each valve and closure time)
window_steps.tag_ref: OPTIONAL: reference isolation valve tags here

window_steps.description: Verify zero pressure at work point; open drain-down/blowoff; confirm main depressurized and draining
Drain-down complete at cut location; residual water managed to dewatering BMPs
Cut existing main; remove spool section; clean and inspect pipe ends
Swab/spray interior of new fittings, pipe ends, and appurtenances with hypochlorite solution per C651 tie-in method
Install tie-in assembly (new fitting/valve/spool); torque couplings and flanges per spec
window_steps.tag_ref: OPTIONAL: reference new valve tag here

window_steps.description: Install joint restraint and thrust protection per drawings; inspector verification before backfill/charge
District re-opens isolation valves slowly per agreed sequence; charge line; bleed air at high points
Visual leak check at all new joints under full pressure
Flush downstream per district direction; verify chlorine residual restored (record reading)
District confirms system restored to normal operation — window formally closed (record time vs. window_end)

post_window_steps.description: Post-shutdown report generated (planned vs. actual, step timestamps, problems logged) and distributed
Any follow-up items (paving, permanent restoration, punch items) logged against the system

contingencies.trigger: Isolation valve fails to hold (main won't depressurize)
contingencies.action: Stop before cutting. Options per pre-agreed plan: secondary valve isolation, line stop, or abort and restore. Abort decision by super + district operator jointly; record decision and time.

contingencies.trigger: Existing main dimension/material differs from pothole data
contingencies.action: Assess adaptability of on-hand fittings within window time budget. If cut has not been made, abort is available; if cut is made, execute fallback coupling plan.

contingencies.trigger: Window overrun projected (any step exceeds planned duration by agreed threshold)
contingencies.action: Notify district operator immediately with revised restore estimate; district decides on window extension vs. temporary restore.
Make excavation and public safe first; restore isolation to stable state; reschedule.
